text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: serving-runtime cluster us-west-2 - 99th pct latency spike + container restarts on node-7. auto-escalation to oncall.
ryan_oncall: I’m on it. grabbing logs and repro window.
elena_sre: saw alert too, metrics show continuous-batcher queue depth jumping from ~200 to >40k over ~3m before OOMs.
matt_runtime: curious — any recent rollout of the batcher config?
ryan_oncall: no prod rollouts in the last 6h per deploy-bot. looks like a sudden growth not tied to deploy.
shreya_prod: customer-impact: a few customers reported 500s and timeouts, CS is triaging. cc @cs_lead
cs_lead: acknowledged — I’ve informed the affected enterprise tenants, flagging as degraded.
elena_sre: stack traces from the crashed containers show repeated CUDA OOM entries followed by container crash loop:```
2025-11-03T21:12:03Z runtime: gpu0: CUDA OOM when allocating 3.2GB
...
panic: bcache: kv-prefetch overflow: pending=41234
```
matt_runtime: that bcache/kv-prefetch line is interesting — if prefetch queue loses acknowledgements we can re-enqueue and create exponential growth.
ryan_oncall: nodes showing flaps: node-7 and node-9 both had kubelet restarts around the same time. kernel logs show GPU reset events on both.
infra-bot: node-7: gpu0 reset, docker restart sequence recorded. node-9: oom_killer invoked, container restarted.
ryan_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable kv-prefetch in continuous-batcher on us-west-2; 2) reduce max_batch_size and max_concurrent_batches; 3) reroute traffic off node-7/9; 4) add rate-limit to heavy customers. executing step 1 now.
elena_sre: how do we disable kv-prefetch at runtime?
matt_runtime: we have a runtime flag: `CONT_BATCHER_PREFETCH_ENABLE=false` per pool; pushing via configstore.
ryan_oncall: running command:```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood/api/admin/configs/us-west-2 -d '{"CONT_BATCHER_PREFETCH_ENABLE":"false"}'
```
ops-bot: configstore change accepted, rolling to 4 pools in us-west-2.
elena_sre: rolling to pools now — watching queue depth.
(30s later)
elena_sre: queue depth stopped climbing, new steady at ~800. CUDA OOM messages decreased.
ryan_oncall: proceeding step 2: lowering `CONT_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH` from 2048 -> 256 and `CONT_BATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT` from 32 -> 8. pushing change.
matt_runtime: also set `KV_PREFETCH_LIMIT=512` to force bounded memory.
ops-bot: runtime flags applied.
ryan_oncall: step 3: cordon and drain node-7, node-9 for deeper investigation, evicting pods to other healthy nodes.
infra-bot: cordon node-7, start drain. Migration in progress.
elena_sre: restarting the most recent container on a clean node to validate no immediate OOM; logs show prefetch backlog didn't rebuild.
shreya_prod: CS update: primary affected customers seeing partial recovery, error rate down from 12% -> 1.8% for those routes. attaching summary to the incident ticket.
ryan_oncall: customer mitigation: applied per-tenant throttles for the top 10 heavy tenants — reduced concurrent requests by 60% to stop surge.
elena_sre: root-cause hypothesis: a race in continuous-batcher ack handling. when a worker fails to ack due to transient GPU reset, the queue re-enqueues the job but the accounting doesn’t decrement, causing unbounded pending count and aggressive prefetch that grows until memory/OOM. we need a guard to avoid re-enqueue loops.
matt_runtime: I can push a hotfix: add an idempotent ack cleanup and a cap on re-enqueue attempts (max 3) + backoff. will cut a PR now and prepare a canary.
ryan_oncall: can we keep the temporary runtime flags (prefetch disabled + small batches) until hotfix is rolled?
matt_runtime: yes. plan: cut PR -> canary in staging -> canary in us-west-2 limited to 5% traffic -> promote. ETA ~90m for canary + validation.
elena_sre: follow-up tasks for postmortem: collect full node kernel logs, GPU reset telemetry, continuous-batcher pending accounting trace around enqueue/dequeue, and list of affected customers + request traces.
ryan_oncall: notifying paging channels and SRE leads. tagging for priority follow-up. handing off to matt_runtime for the code fix; I will remain for any further mitigation for 30m then pass to next oncall.
matt_runtime: accepted handoff. I’ll open the PR and post the link.
(2m later)
matt_runtime: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 - adds re-enqueue cap + ack reconciliation on worker reconnect.
elena_sre: test matrix: synthetic replay with simulated GPU reset shows no runaway backlog after fix.
ryan_oncall: marking incident as mitigated in PagerDuty and updating incident channel. leaving note for postmortem and to follow up with CS for formal customer communique.
cs_lead: thanks — we'll coordinate customer postmortem notes.
matt_runtime: will schedule a canary rollout in ~40m and monitor memory/gpu metrics.
elena_sre: great. last check: any other nodes showing signs? all cleared.
ryan_oncall: closing live coordination. please add to postmortem: timeline, config changes, PR link, and recommended long-term fix (accounting invariants + stronger prefetch caps).
incident-bot: incident status updated: MITIGATED - control plane flags applied. please file postmortem with labels: sev2, continuous-batcher, cuda, node-flap.
